title: Severe Pest Infestation and Lack of Heating in a Family Home
summary: A housing-association tenant and mother of two young children experienced prolonged heating failure followed by serious bedbug and mice infestations.
defects: Four years without functioning living-room heating
Severe bedbug infestation followed by widespread mice activity
Contaminated living areas and damaged belongings
Electrical and other safety concerns requiring remedial work
impact: With no temporary accommodation offered, the family moved between friends’ homes. The tenant reported anxiety and sleep disruption while caring for children aged one and four, and disposed of soft furnishings and other belongings affected by infestation.
work: The housing team assembled evidence, pressed for urgent interim protection, and pursued heating, pest-eradication, proofing, electrical and cleaning work.
outcome: The heating was restored, pest treatment and proofing were completed, electrical safety issues were addressed and the property was professionally cleaned. A settlement was also agreed. The source does not publish the settlement figure.

title: Persistent Bathroom Leak and Water Damage
summary: A private tenant caring for a young child lived with a recurring bathroom leak that caused significant water damage to the kitchen ceiling below.
defects: Persistent bathroom leak
Water-damaged kitchen ceiling and surrounding walls
Temporary sealant repairs that did not stop recurrence
Delayed repair of a broken garden fence
impact: The continuing damp, visible damage and ineffective repairs caused daily disruption and anxiety while the tenant cared for her child.
work: Photographs and the reporting history were organised to demonstrate recurrence and the ineffectiveness of surface repairs. The matter was then presented to the landlord and negotiated.
outcome: The claim concluded with a settlement reflecting the disruption and inconvenience. The source describes the payment as fair but does not publish a figure.

title: Hazardous Flooring Defects and Pest Infestation
summary: A private tenant and young family experienced gaps and holes in flooring alongside a persistent mouse infestation after moving into their home in October 2022.
defects: Gaps and holes creating trip hazards
Unsafe flooring around a young child
Persistent mice infestation
Open floor defects that enabled pest entry
impact: The family experienced continuing anxiety about injury and health risks. The landlord initially blamed the tenants for the pest problem despite the structural defects.
work: The team documented the flooring and infestation, obtained inspection and photographic evidence, and pressed the landlord for remedial action.
outcome: A settlement was agreed and the landlord committed to addressing the disrepair. No settlement figure is published in the source case study.

title: A Decade of Disrepair Affecting a Tenant and Four Children
summary: A long-term private tenant and her four children lived with extensive damp, leaks, unsafe electrics, unstable floors and sanitation failures.
defects: Widespread damp and mould across living areas and bedrooms
Bathroom pipe leaks allowing wastewater through ceilings and walls
Overheating sockets and electrical fires that damaged appliances
Unstable floorboards, a non-functioning toilet and prolonged loss of cold water to a basin
impact: The conditions affected a tenant with asthma and respiratory illness and were associated with repeated illness among the children. Sewage leaks, electrical hazards and the long reporting history caused severe distress.
work: The team compiled photographs, tenancy documents and historic complaints and documented the defects room by room before formally pursuing the landlord.
outcome: The landlord was required to address the defects and a settlement was achieved for the distress and inconvenience. The source does not state the amount.

title: Damp, Mould and Unsafe Electrics in a Young Family’s Home
summary: A private tenant and three young children experienced serious mould, unsafe bathroom electrics, leaks and defective fixtures from shortly after moving in during April 2024.
defects: Black mould affecting ceilings, walls, windows and belongings
Leaking toilet, unsealed bath and unstable bathroom flooring
Exposed and sparking light fittings with inadequate ventilation
Uneven floors, defective sockets, poorly sealed openings and kitchen defects
impact: The tenant described isolation, anxiety and worsening mental health while trying to protect three children from unsafe conditions and damaged belongings.
work: The legal team reviewed extensive correspondence, photographs and videos, set out the landlord’s duties and presented the household’s vulnerability and repair history.
outcome: The landlord was required to complete work to make the home habitable and a settlement was agreed for the prolonged impact. The amount is not published.

title: Vulnerable Household Left Without Heating and Hot Water
summary: A private tenant living with an adult daughter and two sons, one of whom was non-verbal and autistic, faced damp, water ingress and several months without a working boiler.
defects: Extensive damp and mould across walls and ceilings
Rainwater leaking through living-room light fittings
Partial kitchen-ceiling collapse
Complete boiler failure causing loss of heating, hot water and shower facilities
impact: The family relied on portable heaters and travelled elsewhere to shower. At times everyone slept in one room to keep warm. Existing asthma and diabetes were affected, while the disruption was particularly difficult for the autistic family member.
work: Medical context, inspection records, photographs, video and tenancy evidence were combined to demonstrate vulnerability, prolonged notice and risk.
outcome: Outstanding heating, water-ingress and mould work was pursued and a settlement was agreed. The source does not disclose the amount.

title: Elderly Tenant Left Without Hot Water and Fire-Safety Protection
summary: A 72-year-old disabled private tenant experienced six months without hot water, dangerous electrical work, inadequate fire protection and an insecure toilet that caused a fall.
defects: Failed water-heater installation and prolonged hot-water loss
Electrical wiring overheating and catching fire
Missing or inadequate fire doors, fireproofing and smoke alarms
An unsecured toilet associated with a fall and injury
impact: The tenant required hospital treatment and physiotherapy after the fall. Cold, damp, fire risk and aggressive communications were reported to have affected his health, mobility and mental wellbeing.
work: The case used photographs, correspondence, tenancy records and evidence from environmental health and the fire service, with communication adapted for the client’s needs.
outcome: Fire-safety, hot-water and structural issues were pursued and a settlement was reached. The source case study does not publish the figure.

title: Pests and Unsafe Doors in a Housing-Association Flat
summary: A housing-association tenant living in a studio flat reported recurring rats and mice, poorly fitting external doors, mould and concerns about internal construction and fire safety.
defects: Rats and mice entering through floor voids and a disused fireplace
Front and rear doors with gaps affecting security and insulation
Concerns about dividing walls, noise transmission and fire safety
Bathroom mould treated only at surface level
impact: The conditions affected the tenant’s mental health, privacy and sense of security and meant his young son could not safely stay at the property.
work: Complaint responses and repair evidence were organised and the landlord’s obligations were set out in a structured claim.
outcome: The housing association was required to address the infestation and defects, and a settlement was agreed. No figure is published.

title: Respiratory Illness and Years of Recurring Mould
summary: A housing-association tenant with serious respiratory illness experienced recurring damp and mould for years despite earlier rebuilding and surface treatments.
defects: Black mould across living room, kitchen and bedroom areas
Water ingress around windows and suspected roof defects
Earlier wall rebuilding that did not prevent recurrence
Repeated surface spraying without resolving the source
impact: The tenant experienced repeated chest infections, emergency medical assistance and ongoing treatment, alongside anxiety and exhaustion after years of unsuccessful reports.
work: Historic complaints, medical context and records of ineffective work were used to demonstrate duration, vulnerability and the need for a permanent solution.
outcome: The landlord was required to address the underlying causes and a settlement was reached for the prolonged impact. The source does not publish the amount.

title: Years of Boiler Problems and Contractor No-Shows
summary: A council tenant and her family experienced a long-running boiler problem made worse by missed appointments, incorrect contractor attendance and incomplete work.
defects: A defective boiler without a complete service for a prolonged period
Survey and access recommendations not properly coordinated
Wrong or unplanned contractors attending
Family members having to assist with access before partial servicing could take place
impact: Repeatedly preparing for appointments that could not proceed disrupted family life and created stress, privacy concerns and a sense that the household was not being heard.
work: The team clarified the history, secured expert evidence and required coordinated appointments and defined timescales rather than further informal promises.
outcome: The landlord agreed to address the defects within a timetable and a settlement was reached. The source does not state the figure.

title: £2,750 Compensation After a Roof Leak and Widespread Damp
summary: A faulty roof with missing tiles allowed water into a Bicester tenant’s home, causing damp, staining and deterioration across several rooms.
defects: Missing roof tiles and water entering the loft
Cracked and water-stained ceilings
Damp smell and a defective kitchen extractor
Bedroom damp and staining around a window
impact: Recurring leaks, damp smells and concern about moisture spreading into the structure caused continuing disruption and anxiety.
work: The roof defect, internal staining and reporting history were evidenced and presented as one connected water-ingress problem.
outcome: The matter concluded with £2,750 compensation for the prolonged leak, damp and associated disruption.

title: £6,000 Compensation After Leaks and Guttering Caused Severe Damp
summary: A tenant experienced extensive damp and mould associated with roof, guttering and ventilation defects, alongside electrical and safety-related problems.
defects: Damp and mould across several rooms
Defective roof and guttering with vegetation and external moss
Intermittent extraction and defective air vents
Damp-affected electrics, damaged plasterboard and defective safety fittings
impact: Sleeping areas and essential rooms were affected, while concerns about electrics, alarms and ventilation increased the tenant’s anxiety.
work: The internal and external causes were linked through an evidence-led claim and the effect on multiple rooms and essential fittings was documented.
outcome: The matter resolved with £6,000 compensation for the prolonged conditions and their effect on the tenant’s home.

title: £2,000 Compensation Following a Persistent Leak and Worsening Damp
summary: A Hull tenant reported a downstairs leak for an extended period while damp, mould and crumbling plaster continued to spread despite repeated visits.
defects: Long-running downstairs leak
Damp and mould within a kitchen larder and adjacent toilet area
Wet internal walls and deteriorating plaster
Surface mould treatments that did not address the leak
impact: Parts of the downstairs space became difficult to use, while the appearance, smell and repeated ineffective visits caused frustration and distress.
work: The case connected the persistent leak to its internal consequences and demonstrated why cosmetic mould treatment had not resolved the cause.
outcome: The claim concluded with £2,000 compensation for the prolonged leak, damp, mould and disruption.

title: £8,000 Compensation After Water Penetration Caused Extensive Damage
summary: Water penetration and poor weatherproofing affected a Leeds tenant’s external door, windows, walls and several living and sleeping areas.
defects: Failed front-door sealant allowing water ingress
Defective windows and latches causing gaps and draughts
Damp and mould across bedrooms, living room and office space
Bubbling paint and walls that felt damp during winter
impact: The spread of water damage, cold draughts and damp across important rooms caused continuing discomfort, disruption and anxiety.
work: The claim documented the external defects and resulting internal deterioration as a connected pattern of failed weatherproofing.
outcome: The matter resolved with £8,000 compensation for the prolonged water penetration, damp, mould and related defects.

title: £2,000 Compensation for Multiple Defects and Serious Damp
summary: A Sheffield tenant experienced defects across entrances, utility areas, bedrooms and bathrooms, including water ingress, mould, unsafe finishes and recurring roof problems.
defects: A defective front door and seals allowing draughts and water ingress
Mould and fungal growth within a basement utility area
Roof leakage and water penetration into a bedroom ceiling
Defective window seals, damaged flooring, bathroom electrics and sharp cracked tiles
impact: The scale of the defects affected everyday comfort and caused worry about mould, water-damaged electrics and unsafe surfaces throughout the home.
work: The team documented each area, formally presented the full scope of the problem and maintained communication while pressing for a practical resolution.
outcome: The matter concluded with £2,000 compensation for the distress and inconvenience caused by the multiple defects.
